description: A director of people operations must finalize the participation plan for a cross-team retreat intended to improve trust after a merger, including the schedule, facilitation, breakout boundaries, and follow-up commitments.

shared_context.S1: The recently merged Customer Insights and Operations teams are scheduled for a trust-building retreat next month.
shared_context.S2: The current draft describes a full-day in-person event with team discussions, paired exercises, and a manager-led reflection.
shared_context.S3: Mara has authority to approve the final retreat format and participation safeguards.
shared_context.S4: As a routine step before employee events, Mara conducts a round-robin consultation in which each participating team member and HR representative must state any relevant constraint or safeguard before Mara approves the plan.
shared_context.S5: Mara's event-approval checklist requires the final plan to record the agreed safeguards and assign a concrete follow-up commitment for each incident-documentation or post-event check-in action.

PF1.text: Imani has an approved caregiving arrangement for the retreat date: she may participate only remotely, and only during the exact 13:00 through 16:00 window. The retreat cannot require her participation before 13:00 or after 16:00. The arrangement is recorded in her local manager's file but was not attached to the event request.

PF2.text: Leo personally observed exactly two earlier team sessions in which Alex, the Operations manager, publicly interrupted Sam during disagreements. Because the retreat includes exercises involving power differences, Leo asks that the plan record exactly those two observed incidents, prohibit supervisor-employee pairings in the exercises, and include a commitment to document the incidents; he has not filed an incident summary.

PF3.text: Ruth confirmed yesterday that the company's trust-building event procedure requires written opt-in before any conflict-repair exercise, a neutral facilitator, and exactly two follow-up check-ins. The current draft does not include these safeguards, and the procedure memo has not yet been attached to Mara's event packet.

acceptance_conditions: The retreat must be hybrid so Imani can participate remotely.
The retreat must run exactly from 13:00 through 16:00.
The record must contain exactly two observed prior incidents.
Supervisor-employee pairings must be prohibited in the exercises.
A neutral facilitator must lead the retreat.
Written opt-in must be required before the conflict-repair exercise.
Exactly two follow-up check-ins must be scheduled.
The plan must include commitments to document the incident record and schedule the follow-ups.

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF2' in credited_facts and 'PF2' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF2' in revealed

decisive_facts.why: Imani's approved arrangement changes the drafted full-day in-person event to a hybrid retreat running exactly from 13:00 through 16:00, because she cannot participate before 13:00 or after 16:00.
Leo's two firsthand observations change the incident record to exactly 2, prohibit supervisor-employee pairings, and require an incident-documentation commitment naming those two incidents.
Ruth's confirmed procedure changes the retreat plan to a neutral facilitator, written opt-in, and exactly 2 follow-up check-ins with a retreat-follow-up commitment.
